title: ALPHA YY
canon: Written by Mike Diaz in prison, mailed page by page to Marco Caruso (typed 2007, revised in pen 2009). Late-2000s New York — Staten Island and Manhattan's Little Italy: Mike and Dario, enforcers working a loan shark's list of beatings, collections and the odd hit, singing along to the car radio between bodies. An unsanctioned prison-kite job in New Jersey puts Mike's name in the air upstairs, and it is his oldest friend Marco who comes to the door: doorbell, 'Everything's gonna be alright now,' fade out.
look: Mid-2000s New York shot like the American crime pictures it descends from — 35mm, natural grain, muted unglamorous color. Most of the violence happens in flat ordinary daylight: overcast Staten Island streets, plastic-sheeted basements under a bare work bulb, Little Italy awnings under a white sky. Nights are practical-lit only — sodium streetlamps, cafe tungsten, restaurant neon, a porch bulb. The frame stays banal and everyday; the menace is in what the ordinary light falls on.
note: Light Law pass 2026-07-18 — prompts from ALPHA_YY_feature_v3.fdx. Eight new moment-in-time frames (Marco's 2026-07-18 standard: human emotion is the story — a touch, an embrace, a look held too long), none duplicating the twelve shots in specs/11-02-alpha-yy.json or the canonical tower-catwalk hero. Every shot cites its scene from the v3 feature per LIGHT-LAW §1; all light is the location's own per §2. Mike's own 2009 pen drove the script toward the love story (the end card says so), so Big Trouble carries three frames. Refs per current manifest: Mike = Mike.jpg + magicPrison.jpg (shaved-bald, stocky, open shirt over white tank); Dario = dario.jpg; Big Trouble = Argentinian.jpg (presumed likeness, Marco to confirm before batch). John and Father Bobby have no refs — prompts own them. Marco's face is never held (no confirmed ref; housie-mousie.jpg unruled) — he is framed turned away. RULINGS 2026-09-02 (Marco): Argentinian.jpg = Big Trouble STANDS. housie-mousie.jpg is RULED as the face of the antagonist 'Marco' (the neighborhood boss who sends Mike to the door) — 'the face of evil'; his face may now be held in frame with that ref. John and Father Bobby stay prompt-owned.

stills.notes: INT. JOHN'S APARTMENT - LATER (Ep I, A5 domestic beat): 'She carries Anna out. The kid waves at Mike over her mother's shoulder until they're gone. Mike watches the empty doorway a beat too long.' The look held too long IS the story — a killer watching the life he refused walk out of a kitchen.
stills.prompt: Kitchen of a family walk-up apartment on Mulberry Street, Little Italy, Manhattan, 2008, late morning. A stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up shirt over a white tank stands stone still by the counter, a half-eaten buttered roll forgotten in his hand, watching the hallway doorway. In the doorway, mid-exit, a pretty tired young mother with a baby-stain on one shoulder carries a two-year-old girl who waves back at him over her mother's shoulder. The only light is flat white daylight through the single window over the sink, bright on his face and dying fast down the hall, the doorway going to shadow around the mother and child. Toddler toys on the linoleum, a glass ginger-ale bottle on the table. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT. MIKE'S HOUSE - NITE (Ep I, A3 couch scene): 'She's looking at him the way nobody else in this movie ever looks at him — like there's a person under the act.' / 'You could be anybody you wanted.' The want and the refusal in one held look — the exit named, and the shutter coming down behind his eyes.
stills.prompt: Living room of a modest vinyl-sided Staten Island house, 2008, well past midnight. On a worn couch, a beautiful dark-haired young woman sits knees up, swallowed by a man's white tee shirt, hair shower-wet, a half-empty whiskey bottle on the coffee table between her and a stocky, shaved-bald man in boxers and a tank top at the couch's other end. She looks straight at him, soft and absolutely serious, seeing the person under the act; he looks away at nothing, jaw set, the joke gone from his face. The only light: one warm shaded table lamp and the blue flicker of a muted television crossing on their skin, corners of the room fully dark, window black behind thin curtains. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT: MIKES BEDROOM / MORNING (Ep II): 'Mike sleeps with his arm protectively over BIG TROUBLE, she is sleeping beauty in his arms.' / 'Suddenly, she wakes up to the SOUND of WEED WHACKERS.' The one unguarded tenderness in the picture — a protective arm from a man who hurts people for a living, seconds before the morning breaks it.
stills.prompt: Small bedroom of a vinyl-sided Staten Island house, 2008, seven in the morning. Hard low sun blasts through cheap venetian blinds, striping the bed in blown-out white bars and deep shadow. A stocky, shaved-bald man lies asleep on his side, face slack and harmless on the pillow, one heavy arm laid protectively over a beautiful dark-haired young woman tucked against his chest; her eyes have just opened toward the burning window, his have not. Tangled sheets, an alarm clock, a full ashtray and a glass of water on the nightstand, clothes over a chair. The window itself flares to pure white; where the sun bars miss, the room falls to brown dark. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT: JOHN'S APARTMENT / LATER (Ep II): 'John grabs Mikes head and pushes him into the wall, hard.' / 'Nothing from the the [sic] wasteland and nothing off a kite!' / 'I'm sorry but everything is not play.' A brother's terror wearing the shape of violence — the grip is love, and Mike will defy it anyway.
stills.prompt: Kitchen of a family walk-up on Mulberry Street, Little Italy, Manhattan, 2008, afternoon. A heavyset man in his forties in a t-shirt has both hands clamped on the head of a stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up over a white tank, pressing it against the painted plaster wall, their faces inches apart — one face all fear dressed as fury, the other gone cold. The bald man's hands stay down at his sides; he does not fight his brother. A child's crayon drawing hangs crooked beside their heads. Hard side daylight from the single kitchen window rakes across both men, the far halves of their faces falling into shadow, the hallway behind them dim. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT: JOHN'S HOUSE - NIGHT (Ep II, A6): 'He stops at the BABY'S CLOSET. Opens it slow so it doesn't creak.' / 'the gun lives wrapped in a hanky. He looks at it a long time.' / 'Then he looks back down the hall at the kids' door.' Six feet of plaster between a loaded gun and his sleeping children — a father doing the arithmetic he can't undo. No ref exists for John; the prompt owns him.
stills.prompt: Narrow hallway of a Little Italy walk-up apartment, Manhattan, 2008, deep night, everyone asleep. A heavyset man in his forties, undershirt and sock feet, stands at an open closet — high shelf stacked with folded baby onesies and a diaper box, and pushed behind them a small heavy bundle wrapped in a white handkerchief. He is not looking at the bundle: his head is turned back down the dark hall toward a children's bedroom door standing ajar, a dim plug-in nightlight glowing at the floor inside. The only other light is the cold greenish spill of the kitchen fluorescent from the far end of the hall, edging his shoulder and cheek and leaving most of his face dark. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT. THE USUAL SPOT (Ep III): 'He leans over on her as she embraces him with her arms over his chest.' / 'Please, don't go. You can take everything you have and make a new life for yourself.' / 'They rest quietly in each others arms.' The embrace is the whole plea — the one chance out, held in her arms and already refused. The usual spot is their cafe on Avenue A.
stills.prompt: Window table inside a small East Village cafe on Avenue A, Manhattan, 2008, night, near closing. A stocky, shaved-bald man in an open button-up over a white tank leans back into a beautiful dark-haired young woman in a leather jacket; her arms are wrapped over his chest from behind, her cheek pressed to his temple, eyes shut, holding on. His eyes are open, fixed on the middle distance, a man already gone somewhere she can't follow. Two espressos untouched. All the light belongs to the room: warm tungsten pendants and the espresso machine's glow, the plate glass beside them black except for one green-white streetlamp through the park trees and their own faint reflection. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT. DARIO'S HOUSE - NIGHT, GEARING UP shot F (Ep III): 'Dario, in the hall mirror, takes his time. Fixes his hair. Smooths one eyebrow with a wet thumb.' / 'the story they need to tell themselves tonight is that it's just a meeting.' A man armed for an invasion grooming for a date — the lie he needs, met in his own eyes.
stills.prompt: Hallway of a Staten Island rowhouse, 2008, night. In an oval wall mirror, a lean dark-haired man meets his own eyes as he smooths one eyebrow with a wet thumb, taking his time, vain and careful — while under his ordinary shirt his torso is bulked square by a ballistic vest and two pistol grips ride his waistband. Behind him, through the kitchen doorway, the mirror also catches a table lined with pistols laid barrels-out and loaded magazines under a bare ceiling bulb. The hall is lit by one small warm wall sconce; the kitchen bulb is harsher and greener, the two mixing on his shoulders. His reflected face is calm, almost tender with itself. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EXT: GUN SHOP / GRAND AND MULBERRY - DAY (Ep II, A9): 'He's turned half away, one hand cupped over the phone like he's shielding a match in wind.' / ''He's a good earner, that's all I'm sayin'. But it's your call.'' The neighborhood boss made small — a man taking instruction, already defending Mike to the voice that will one day send him to the door. No refs: Marco's face is never held; he is framed from behind, face away.
stills.prompt: The corner of Grand and Mulberry, Little Italy, Manhattan, 2008, late morning under hard high sun. Seen from behind across the sidewalk, a broad, well-dressed man stands turned into the recessed doorway of a small gun shop, steel gate half raised, his head bowed and one hand cupped around the phone at his ear as if shielding a match in wind; a paper envelope hangs from his other hand. His face stays hidden in the doorway's deep shade while the noon sun burns white on the sidewalk and parked cars behind him. Down the block, red-white-green awnings, an old man with a folding chair, delivery boxes at a curb — the street he runs, going on without him while he listens. Shot on 35mm film, mid-2000s American crime picture, muted unglamorous color, natural grain, full-bleed frame. No text, no watermark.
